sentences.text:
The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.Nos. 859 Of 2019 And 888 Of 2019
Common Judgment

:
These two appeals are being disposed of by this common judgment since M.A.C.M.A.No. 859 of 2019, filed by the New India Assurance Company Limited and M.A.C.M.A.No. 888 of 2019 filed by claimant challenging the quantum of compensation, are directed against the very same judgment and decree, dated 09.09.2009 made in M.V.O.P.No. 635 of 2006 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Warangal (for short "the Tribunal").
2.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Warangal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, hereinafter the parties will be referred to as per their array before the Tribunal.

3. The facts, in brief, are that the claimant laid a claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, claiming compensation of Rs.7,05,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the accident that occurred on 05.06.2002.

It is stated that on that fateful day while the claimant was travelling in Jeep bearing No. AP Q 904 and at about 07:30 hours when he reached near Jagital RTC bus depot,
one bus bearing No. AP 36 U 3555, owned by respondent No.1, insured with respondent No.2, hired by respondent No.3, being driven by its driver, came in a rash and 2 MGP, J Macma_859_2019 and 888_2019 negligent manner at high speed and dashed the claimant.
As a result, the claimant sustained grievous and multiple injuries and immediately, he was taken to Civil Hospital, Jagital and later, shifted to MGM Hospital, Warangal.
On a complaint, a case in Crime No. 122 of 2002 was registered under Section 337 IPC.
According to the claimant, he was hale and healthy and earning Rs.4,000/- per month as driver.
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered with permanent disability and lost his earning capacity.

Therefore, he laid the claim against the respondent Nos.1 to 3.
4.

Before the Tribunal, respondent No.1 filed counter denying the petition averments, including the manner in which the accident took place, age, avocation and earnings of the injured and also contended that since the policy is in force as on the date of the accident, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2 filed counter stating that there is contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the jeep in which the injured was travelling.
Hence, the respondent No. 2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

On the other hand, respondent No. 3 filed counter contending that respondent No.3 is only hirer of the bus and in view of existence of Ex.B1 policy, 3 MGP, J Macma_859_2019 and 888_2019 respondent Nos. 1 and 2, being the owner and insurer, are liable to pay the compensation and prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. The Tribunal, on examining the oral and documentary evidence brought on record, partly allowed the O.P. awarding a total compensation of Rs.1,53,086/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs K Shahan Baba And 2 Others on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23256762/
1 the date of petition till the date of realization, to be paid by the respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein being owner and insurer jointly and severally within one month from the date of said order while dismissing the claim against respondent No.3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Challenging the same, the present Appeals came to be filed by the Insurance Company and the claimant respectively.

6. Heard both the learned counsel and perused the material available on record.
7.

The main contention raised by the learned Standing Counsel for the New India Assurance Company Limited (appellant in M.A.C.M.A.No. 859 of 2019) is that although the claimant failed to prove his income by producing cogent and documentary evidence, the Tribunal erred in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.2,490.75 per month.
Therefore, the Tribunal has granted excessive and exorbitant compensation, which needs to be reduced.

Per contra, learned counsel for the claimant (appellant in M.A.C.M.A.No. 888 of 2019), has contended that the claimant has asserted that he was earning Rs.4,000/- per month as driver but the Tribunal has erroneously fixed the income of the claimant at Rs.2,490.75.

He further contended that although the claimant, by way of medical evidence i.e. the evidence of P.W. 2, doctor, coupled with Ex.A.2, Injury certificate, sufficiently established that the claimant had sustained disability at 80% due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, the Tribunal has estimated the disability at 30% thereby awarded meager amount towards loss of income due to disability.
Therefore, prayed to enhance the compensation.

9. As regards the manner of accident, the Tribunal has framed issue No.1 as to whether the injured sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of driver of bus bearing No. AP 36 U 3555, and after considering the evidence of P.W.1 coupled with the documentary evidence i.e., Ex.A1, First Information Report and Ex.A3, charge sheet, the Tribunal has categorically observed that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle i.e., bus by its driver and has answered the issue in favour of the claimant and against the respondents.

Therefore, I see no reason to interfere with the finding of the Tribunal that 5 MGP, J Macma_859_2019 and 888_2019 the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.

10. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the case of claimant is that he was earning Rs.4,000/- per month as driver and due to the alleged accident, he suffered with 80% permanent disability as his right leg was amputated below right knee and lost his earning capacity.
However, in support of his claim, no oral or documentary evidence is adduced to show that he was driver by profession.
Further, he did not file disability certificate issued by medical board or the doctor who treated him.
Hence, considering the evidence available on record, the Tribunal has rightly fixed the disability at 30%.
Based on Ex.A.6, bunch of medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly awarded Rs.15,486/- towards medical expenses, which needs no interference.
Duly taking into consideration the prevailing rate of minimum wages during the year 2002, this Court is inclined to fix the income of the claimant at Rs.3,500/- per month.

Further, as the age of the injured was aged between 21 to 25 years at the time of the accident, the appropriate multiplier is '18' as per the decision reported in The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs K Shahan Baba And 2 Others on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23256762/
2 Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation1.

sentences.text: Adopting multiplier 18, the total loss of income due to disability 2009 ACJ 1298 (SC) 6 MGP, J Macma_859_2019 and 888_2019 works out to Rs.2,26,800/- (Rs.3,500/- x 12 x 18 x 30/100).

That apart, the amount of Rs.10,000/- each for three fracture injuries which are grievous in nature as per Ex.A.2, Injury certificate, awarded by the Tribunal appears to be meager and the same can be enhanced to Rs.15,000/- each.

Further, no amount is awarded for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges, hence, a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges; Rs.25,000/-
towards pain and suffering is awarded.
Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled to Rs.3,37,286/-.
11. Coming to the issue of liability for payment of compensation, the respondent No.3-RTC is the hirer of the crime bus that belonged to respondent No. 1 and insured with respondent No. 2.
Admittedly, Ex.B.1 policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The owner of the bus paid the premium towards liability of passengers and third party's risk.
The insurance company collected the said premium and issued Ex.B1 policy.
Once the insurance company collected the premium covering the risk to the passengers and third parties, it is no longer open to the insurance company to escape their liability.

Since the offending bus was covered by Ex.B1 policy even though subsequently hired to RTC, the insurance company would not 7 MGP, J Macma_859_2019 and 888_2019 escape from its liability so far as third parties/victims are concerned.

On principle, it is not open to the insurance company to absolve its liability towards passengers/third party risk on the short ground that the insured vehicle has been given on hire (refer to Ch. Maruthi v. Porandla Susheela in MACMA No.
4669 of 2008, dated 24.11.2017).

sentences.text: In view of the above, the Tribunal was right in exonerating the respondent No. 3-RTC from the liability of payment of compensation and directing the respondent No. 2- Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount and the said findings needs no interference by this Court.

12. Insofar as the interest awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, in light of the decision of the Apex Court in Rajesh and others v. Rajbir Singh and others2 the rate of interest is hereby enhanced from 6% to 7.5% per annum on the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from the date of petition till the date of realization.

entities.text: Rajesh and others v. Rajbir Singh and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In the result, while dismissing the MACMA No. 859 of 2019, the MACMA No. 888 of 2019 is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.1,53,086.40 to Rs.3,37,286/- to be paid by respondent No.2.

The enhanced 2 2013 ACJ 1403 = 2013 (4) ALT 35 8 MGP, J Macma_859_2019 and 888_2019 amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization The said amount shall be deposited within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
